linked_issues.title: `gh auth status` reports rate limit / network failures as "token is invalid" with misleading re-auth advice
linked_issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`gh auth status` reports "The token in `<source>` is invalid." for **any** token-validation failure, not just 401 Unauthorized. A 403 rate-limit response, a 5xx, or a TLS/DNS failure all produce the same misleading message plus a "To re-authenticate, run: gh auth refresh" hint that is useless (or actively harmful) for non-auth failures.

In `pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go`, `buildEntry` only special-cases network timeouts; every other error collapses into `authEntryStateError`, and `authEntry.String` unconditionally renders "The token in %s is invalid." for that state — the actual error is only visible via `--json hosts` (`entry.error`).

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Exhaust the account's API rate limit (e.g. an agent/CI loop hitting the API, or a shared token used by another process).
2. Run `gh auth status`.

Actual output:

```
github.com
  X Failed to log in to github.com account <user> (keyring)
  - Active account: true
  - The token in keyring is invalid.
  - To re-authenticate, run: gh auth refresh -h github.com
  - To forget about this account, run: gh auth logout -h github.com -u <user>
```

3. The token is actually fine: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.github.com/user` returns `403` with `API rate limit exceeded for user ID ...`, and succeeds again once the limit resets — no re-authentication involved.

### Expected vs actual behavior

**Expected:** distinguish 401 (genuinely invalid/revoked token → "invalid" + re-auth hint) from other failures (rate limit, server error, network), and surface the real error — e.g. "Could not verify token: API rate limit exceeded for user ID ...".

**Actual:** every failure is reported as an invalid token, and the suggested fix (`gh auth refresh`) does nothing for rate limits — refreshing while rate limited makes the validation request fail again, so the situation appears worse.

### Additional context

- gh version 2.96.0; same code on `trunk`.
- Related: #8293 — timeouts used to be misreported the same way and received a dedicated `timeout` state; this issue is the same class of problem for every other error type.
- The detail is already collected (`entry.Error`) but only exposed through `--json hosts`; a status-code-aware message in the human-readable output would resolve this.

issues.description: The underlying error is printed only when stderr is a TTY (opts.IO.IsStderrTTY()), so `gh auth status` behaves differently for TTY and non-TTY output, and the error line is rendered outside authEntry.String instead of like the other entry lines. Fixed by moving it into authEntry.String for both modes.

prs.author: YAshhh29
prs.title: Support Pydantic structured outputs in OpenAIResponseOperator
prs.body:
This adds structured outputs to `OpenAIResponseOperator`. If you pass a Pydantic model as `text_format`, the operator calls `OpenAIHook.parse_response` (a thin wrapper around the SDK's `responses.parse`) and returns the parsed result as a plain dict via `model_dump(mode="json")`, so it's safe to push to XCom. Without `text_format`, nothing changes.

```python
class Person(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int

OpenAIResponseOperator(
    task_id="extract_person",
    conn_id="openai_default",
    input_text="Extract the name and age from: 'Alice is 30 years old'.",
    text_format=Person,
)
```

**When something goes wrong, the task fails instead of passing partial data downstream:**
- the response didn't complete (for example it hit `max_output_tokens`), even if the partial JSON happens to validate
- there's no parsed output, like a refusal or a response that only made tool calls
- the SDK can't parse the output at all (usually truncation), in which case its `ValidationError` becomes a `ValueError` that names the model

The error includes the response id and whatever the API sent back: status, error, incomplete details, the refusal text or the output item types.

**It fits the rest of the operator.** `max_output_tokens`, `max_tool_calls` and `response_kwargs` work the same for structured requests, and `response_id` and `usage` are pushed to XCom for both paths. For structured responses they're pushed before the output is checked, so even a rejected response records what it cost. `text_format` is keyword-only and checked when the operator is created, because the SDK also accepts pydantic dataclasses, which would only fail after the paid API call.

**Testing**
- Unit tests pass on openai 2.37.0, 2.46.0 and 2.54.0
- End-to-end through a real `OpenAIHook` and SDK client with only the HTTP layer faked: success, refusal, incomplete-but-valid, truncated JSON, a failed response and the plain-text path
- I removed each safeguard one at a time to make sure a test catches it
- An earlier version ran live against the OpenAI API on a from-source main build (screenshots in the comments below)

---

issues.description: The structured output is returned via model_dump() in python mode, so a model with a plain enum.Enum (or other non-JSON) field yields live Python objects that fail at XCom push with a serialization TypeError after the paid API call. The fix commit switched to model_dump(mode="json").

The `output_parsed is None` check claims to cover truncated responses, but on truncated JSON responses.parse() raises pydantic.ValidationError inside parse_response before `parsed` exists, so users get a raw traceback with no response id and the intended error never fires. The fix commit wraps the parse_response call in try/except ValidationError and re-raises a shaped ValueError.

prs.title: Provisioning: render mermaid diagrams in folder README
prs.body:
## What Mermaid diagrams (` ```mermaid ` fenced code blocks) in a provisioned folder's `README.md` now render as actual diagrams in the folder view, instead of showing as raw code. - Diagrams are themed to match Grafana light/dark mode. - A diagram that fails to parse keeps its source visible and is flagged, rather than hiding the rest of the README. ## Why The Folder README feature (`provisioning.readmes`) renders GitHub-style READMEs inline. GitHub renders mermaid fences as diagrams, so authors reasonably expect the same here — but the existing pipeline (`marked` → sanitize → `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) left them as `
` blocks.

## How
- New util `public/app/features/provisioning/utils/mermaid.ts`: `renderMermaidDiagrams()` scans the already-rendered README DOM for `code.language-mermaid` blocks and replaces each `
` with the rendered SVG.
  - **Lazy-loaded**: `mermaid` is pulled in via dynamic `import()` only when a README actually contains a diagram, so it lands in its own webpack chunk and does not bloat the main bundle (no-op / no import otherwise).
  - **Safe**: initialized with `securityLevel: 'strict'`, so mermaid sanitizes its own SVG and disables interactivity — safe despite bypassing the README's outer sanitizer.
  - Per-diagram error handling with `suppressErrorRendering: true`.
- `FolderReadmePanel.tsx` (`RenderedMarkdown`): runs the renderer in an effect after HTML injection (with a `cancelled` signal for cleanup), themed via `useTheme2()`. The container is `key`ed by theme so a light/dark switch resets to source markup and re-renders. Added styles to center diagrams / make SVGs responsive.
- Added `mermaid` `11.16.0` (pinned, matching the repo's exact-version convention).

## Testing
- `yarn jest .../FolderReadmePanel.test.tsx` — 21/21 pass, including 3 new tests (mermaid mocked): renders a diagram and removes the code block; flags + preserves source on render failure; does not load mermaid when there are no diagrams.
- `yarn typecheck` — passes.
- `yarn eslint` on the changed files — clean.
- Manual: on a provisioned folder with `provisioning.readmes` enabled, add a ` ```mermaid ` block to its `README.md`.

## Notes for reviewers
- `mermaid` is a sizeable dependency (d3/cytoscape/etc.), which is why it's dynamically imported into its own chunk rather than added to the main bundle. License is MIT.
- Frontend-only change (consistent with the separate-PR guidance).

prs.title: owens_t: evaluate numerically by direct mpmath quadrature
prs.body:
A timeout issue I've noticed in other PRs. 

`owens_t` was introduced recently during GSoC 2026, so this is probably something we want to fix before the next SymPy release.

#### References to other Issues or PRs

Follow-up of #30347 (`bde8a69ccd`, "Fix precision loss in owens_t evalf"), whose `test_owent_evalf_cancellation` times out on CI.

#### Brief description of what is fixed or changed

`test_owent_evalf_cancellation` has been failing on master with `Failed: Timeout (>10.0s)` (e.g. run 33671000501). The expression `erf(-3*sqrt(2))/2 + 1/2 - 2*owens_t(-6, 2)` cancels down to `7.1e-43`, so `Add` retries the evaluation at increasing precision (eight times, from 67 to 207 bits). Each retry re-evaluated `owens_t` by rewriting it as an `Integral` and running the quadrature through the generic `evalf` machinery, which evaluates the symbolic integrand at every node: 2.3 s locally, and over the 10 s limit on a loaded runner.

`owens_t._eval_evalf` now evaluates the defining integral

$$T(h, a) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^a \frac{e^{-h^2(1+t^2)/2}}{1+t^2}\,dt$$

directly with `mpmath.quad` at the requested precision (plus guard bits), returning `None` for symbolic arguments as before. The cancellation test takes 0.07 s, and the whole `owens_t` test group 0.8 s. Values agree with the previous `Integral` path at 30 digits for real, negative, large, tiny and complex arguments.

#### Other comments

`test_kane.py::test_implicit_kinematics` shows the same timeout pattern on master and is unrelated to this change.

prs.author: asmeurer
prs.title: integrals: fix the floor terms added to atan(tan) and atan(cot) antiderivatives
prs.body:
Integral.doit() adds floor terms to antiderivatives containing
`atan(c*tan(a) + d)` or `atan(c*cot(a) + d)` to cancel the jumps of the atan
at the poles of tan(a) and cot(a). The term that was added was wrong in
several cases, each of which introduced a discontinuity into the
antiderivative and gave wrong definite integrals:

- The term for cot had the wrong sign, which doubled the jump instead of
  canceling it. integrate(diff(atan(2*cot(x)), x), (x, -1, 1)) was
  positive for a negative integrand.

- A coefficient c depending on the integration variable was accepted
  even if its sign changes, giving a term like
  `sign(x)*pi*floor((x - pi/2)/pi)`, which jumps where c changes sign.
  `integrate(diff(atan(x*tan(x)), x), (x, -1, 1))` gave `-2*pi` instead of `0`.
  Such a coefficient is now only accepted if its sign is the same for all
  real values, as in `atan(exp(x)*tan(x))`.

- tan and cot not depending on the integration variable were corrected
  too, so that `integrate(atan(tan(y)), x)` was not `x*atan(tan(y))`.

- With several tan or cot in the argument, each one was corrected
  separately, which corrects a pole that they have in common more than
  once, as at x = pi/2 for atan(tan(x) + tan(3*x)). Now those with the
  same poles are corrected by a single term, and two with different
  periods that have some poles in common get an additional floor term
  for the common poles, where the jump of the atan is given by the sign
  of the sum of the two poles. `atan(tan(x) + tan(3*x))` needs
  `pi*floor((3*x - pi/2)/pi)` only. The argument must also be jointly
  linear in the tan and cot.

An atan for which the floor terms cannot be determined (a coefficient
that changes sign or is not real, poles in common among more than two tan or cot, or
poles that cannot be compared) is left uncorrected. Definite integrals
over its poles are then wrong, as they are for other discontinuous
antiderivatives, since Integral.doit() does not check for those.

The pass is moved to its own function, _add_atan_floor_terms().

The coefficient is only rejected when is_extended_real is False, so when its realness is unknown sign(coeff) is applied anyway and an unjustified floor term is added. The fix commit requires coeff.is_extended_real to be True.

_add_atan_floor_terms corrects jumps along the real axis but is applied whether or not the integration variable is real (e.g. indefinite integrals over a plain Symbol). The fix commit returns the antiderivative unchanged unless x.is_extended_real, so only real-variable (definite) integrals get the correction.

prs.title: feat(bundler): add statically-analyzable dead-code elimination via feature flags
prs.body:
## Summary
- Adds `import { feature } from "bun:bundle"` for compile-time feature flag checking
- `feature("FLAG_NAME")` calls are replaced with `true`/`false` at bundle time
- Enables dead-code elimination through `--feature=FLAG_NAME` CLI argument
- Works in `bun build`, `bun run`, and `bun test`
- Available in both CLI and `Bun.build()` JavaScript API

## Usage

```ts
import { feature } from "bun:bundle";

if (feature("SUPER_SECRET")) {
  console.log("Secret feature enabled!");
} else {
  console.log("Normal mode");
}
```

### CLI
```bash
# Enable feature during build
bun build --feature=SUPER_SECRET index.ts

# Enable at runtime
bun run --feature=SUPER_SECRET index.ts

# Enable in tests
bun test --feature=SUPER_SECRET
```

### JavaScript API
```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ['./index.ts'],
  outdir: './out',
  features: ['SUPER_SECRET', 'ANOTHER_FLAG'],
});
```

## Implementation
- Added `bundler_feature_flags` (as `*const bun.StringSet`) to `RuntimeFeatures` and `BundleOptions`
- Added `bundler_feature_flag_ref` to Parser struct to track the `feature` import
- Handle `bun:bundle` import at parse time (similar to macros) - capture ref, return empty statement
- Handle `feature()` calls in `e_call` visitor - replace with boolean based on flags
- Wire feature flags through CLI arguments and `Bun.build()` API to bundler options
- Added `features` option to `JSBundler.zig` for JavaScript API support
- Added TypeScript types in `bun.d.ts`
- Added documentation to `docs/bundler/index.mdx`

- [x] Multiple feature flags test
- [x] Dead code elimination verification tests
- [x] Error handling for invalid arguments
- [x] Runtime tests with `bun run --feature=FLAG`

prs.title: feat(dotcom): show agent comments with an agent byline
prs.body:
Stacked on #11226. A comment an agent posts through the MCP server is authored by the agent's owner, so today the byline credits the owner alone: "Max", with nothing saying an agent wrote it. This PR uses the `CommentByline` slot (#11447) so tldraw.com shows those comments as the agent's, on the owner's behalf.

An agent comment now reads **Claude** / max, with "/ max" in grey and "On behalf of max" in its tooltip. The avatar follows the design file: the owner's usual 12px avatar with a 9px agent badge over its bottom-right corner, ringed in the panel colour.

- **Branded badge:** Claude's mark, or OpenAI's for ChatGPT and Codex (both from Simple Icons, which has no separate Codex or ChatGPT mark), on a panel-coloured circle.
- **Generic badge:** a grey circle with two white eyes, for an agent with any other name.

The byline now draws every comment, not only agents', so two changes apply to everyone on tldraw.com:

- **The time sits at the right edge.** A thread card's hover actions sit in that spot, so the time fades out while they show. The toolkit's right padding for those actions comes back on hover too, so a long name still stops short of them.
- **An edit shows as tldraw's pencil icon** (`tool-pencil`, labelled "Edited") a few pixels after the time, instead of "· edited".

**Long names on hover.** While a card's actions show, the hidden time now leaves the byline row instead of still taking its width, which cut long names like "Doodlebug / Max Drake" short.

**Sidebar rows and pins.** A thread an agent started gets the same treatment in the comments sidebar (through the `ThreadRow` slot: "Claude / max" and the badged avatar) and on its canvas pin (through `PinContent`, with a slightly larger badge on the 22px avatar). The pin needs the author resolver, which `CommentsOnCanvas` now provides through `ResolveCommentAuthorContext`.

**How a comment is recognised as an agent's.** #11226 stamps an MCP comment's `meta.mcpAgent` with the agent's `{ id, name, client }`, and this PR reads it with `getMcpAgentFromCommentMeta` from `@tldraw/dotcom-shared`. Comments without that meta get the person byline.

**Only the MCP server can badge a comment.** The comment authorizers never looked at `meta`, so a client could have set `meta.mcpAgent` on its own comments and posted as an agent. `authorizeFileRecord` now refuses a client write that adds `meta.mcpAgent` or changes it. Keeping it unchanged or dropping it is still allowed. The MCP write stamps it after the authorizers have passed the comment, so agents still can.

**Decisions to check:**

- **The logo comes from `client`, not the name.** The server reads `client` from the agent's OAuth client id, so a model that calls itself "Claude" from another app gets the generic face, and a real Claude with a custom name keeps Claude's mark. Cursor has no mark here and gets the generic face too.
- **Notifications are left out.** The sidebar's notifications panel builds its rows from Zero, and comment `meta` is a server-only column that never replicates to the client, so the panel can't tell an agent's comment from its owner's without a schema change.

### API changes

- `CommentingComponents.ThreadRow` in `@tldraw/commenting` now also receives `comments: TLComment[]`, the thread's live comments, oldest first, as `PinContent` and `ThreadActions` already do. A row that reads comment `meta` no longer has to subscribe to the store itself.

Behaviour changes in `@tldraw/commenting`, with no API change:

- A card's actions show on keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`) rather than any focus inside the card, and an open menu's trigger is shaded.
- Leaving an edit returns focus to the card's ⋯ button as keyboard focus only when the edit ended from the keyboard (Escape or Enter), with a focus ring on the card's action buttons. After a click on Save the actions stay hidden once the pointer leaves.

### Change type

- [x] `feature`

### Test plan

1. With #11226 deployed, have an agent call `write_comment` on a board, then open the thread on tldraw.com: the comment reads "<agent> / <you>" with your avatar and the agent badge, in light and dark mode. Pass an `agentName` the logos don't know to see the generic badge.
2. Open the hover preview and a stacked list: the same byline shows. For a thread the agent started, check its sidebar row and its pin.
3. Check a person's comment and an edited comment: the time at the right edge, the pencil for the edit, and the time fading out while you hover a card in an open thread.
4. Give an agent a 40-character name: its name truncates and "/ <you>" stays visible.
5. Edit a comment from the ⋯ menu with the keyboard and press Escape: focus lands on the ⋯ button with a ring.
6. From the browser console, try to set `meta.mcpAgent` on your own comment: the write is rejected.

### Release notes

- Show comments an agent posted through the tldraw.com MCP server with the agent's name and who it acted for.

The fix commit adds a server-side comment authorizer that vetoes client writes that add or change meta.mcpAgent.

The agent name (up to 40 chars, chosen by the agent) and the '/ owner' suffix share one ellipsized span, so a long agent name truncates away the real author. The fix commit truncates only the agent name and keeps the owner suffix from shrinking.

prs.title: [Data] Keep tensor columns with null rows mergeable across blocks
prs.body:
## Summary

A batch that spans blocks whose tensor column is null in one of them fails with "Trying to unify unsupported tensor type: null". This PR lets tensor arrays carry null rows, so such blocks merge and the column stays a tensor column, with `None` for the missing rows. A column that is a tensor in one block and pickled objects in another keeps raising; a follow-up PR extends that error with the columns and types found.

## Problem

- Since #61733 (2.56), the batch a pandas UDF returns becomes an Arrow block right away. Each one-row block types a column from its own value: a stacked array becomes a tensor, `None` becomes null.
- Merging those blocks into a batch reconciles the schemas. A tensor with a null arm passed reconciliation and then failed in the tensor unifier, which rejected null.
- Tensor arrays could already hold null rows, but `to_numpy()` on them failed with "buffer is too small", so nothing could read them (#67200).
- In 2.55 the batches stayed pandas blocks, so there was no Arrow schema to unify.

```python
import numpy as np, ray

def decode(batch):
    row = int(batch["id"][0])
    return {"img": [None if row == 5 else np.full((2, 2), row, np.float32)]}

ds = ray.data.range(8).map_batches(decode, batch_size=1)
next(iter(ds.iter_batches(batch_size=8, batch_format="numpy")))
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| 2.55 | works |
| 2.56 to master | `ValueError: Trying to unify unsupported tensor type: null` |
| After | works, `img` is a tensor column with `None` in row 5 |

## Change

```
block 1   img = stacked array   -> tensor
block 2   img = None            -> null

Before:  unify schemas  ->  tensor  ->  concat: "unsupported tensor type: null"
After:   unify schemas  ->  tensor  ->  null chunk becomes null rows of the tensor type
```

- `unify_tensor_arrays` turns a null-typed chunk into null rows of the unified tensor type, so `concat` keeps the column a tensor column.
- Both tensor array classes read null rows: `to_numpy()` returns one ndarray view per row with `None` for each null row, and `from_numpy()` accepts `None` among the tensors. A variable-shaped row is null when its struct slot or either child is null. Null rows survive promotion to the variable-shaped type.
- `TensorArray` accepts `None` rows, so such a column converts to pandas and back.
- The torch conversion error names `None` rows instead of blaming ragged shapes.
- A column that is a tensor in one block and pickled objects in another still raises "Found columns with both objects and tensors". Merging them would silently turn every row into a pickled object and lose the type.

What a batch looks like, for a tensor column where one row is missing:

| batch | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| no missing row | error | `float32 (8, 2, 2)` |
| one missing row | error | `object (8,)`, views and `None`, nothing pickled |
| schema | error | tensor |

## Decisions to confirm

- A batch holding a null row comes back as one ndarray per row with `None`, since a dense array has no slot for a missing row. Filling the row with zeros or NaN would invent data and has no form for integer or ragged tensors.
- `from_numpy()` with `None` among the tensors now builds a tensor array with null rows. Before, such a column fell back to pickled objects with a warning.
- Tensors next to pickled objects keep raising rather than merging to objects, per review. Users make every row the same kind, for example by returning ragged arrays as nested lists.

## Subsystems

Block / data format (`arrow_ops/transform_pyarrow.py`, `tensor_extensions/arrow.py`, `tensor_extensions/pandas.py`).

## Related

- Reported by a customer upgrading from 2.55 to 2.59, alongside #67566.
- Fixes #67200: `to_pandas()` and numpy batches now return `None` for a null tensor row instead of another row's value or an error.
- Overlaps #67236, which makes the same two `to_numpy` paths null-aware and makes `to_pandas` raise on null rows. This PR also builds tensor arrays from input holding `None`, converts null rows to pandas and back, keeps them through shape promotion, and merges null chunks. The rule that a null child marks a null row is taken from #67236.
- Leaves the native `fixed_shape_tensor` type alone; #67293 covers its null rows.
- A follow-up PR extends the objects-and-tensors error with the columns and types found.

## Testing

```
pytest python/ray/data/tests/unit/test_transform_pyarrow.py \
       python/ray/data/tests/test_transform_pyarrow.py \
       python/ray/data/tests/test_arrow_block.py \
       python/ray/data/tests/test_tensor_extension.py \
       python/ray/data/tests/test_torch_tensor_utils.py            # 387 passed
```

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the root cause and write this change.

linked_issues.title: [Data] `to_pandas()` returns another row's value or raises for null rows in tensor columns
linked_issues.body:
### What happened + What you expected to happen

When a tensor column has a null row (for example, after a left outer join where a row has no match), `take_all()` returns `None` for that row, but `to_pandas()` and `iter_batches(batch_format="numpy" | "pandas")` don't.

For a variable-shaped tensor column, the null row comes back as a value taken from another row's data (`20.0` in the reproduction below). On NumPy >= 2.3 the same call raises `TypeError: Use () not None as shape arguments` instead.

For a fixed-shape tensor column, the conversion raises `TypeError: buffer is too small for requested array` on both NumPy versions I tried (2.2.6 and 2.5.4).

I expected the null row to come back as missing, as it does in `take_all()` and for a plain `list<double>` column (`None` in numpy batches, `<NA>` in pandas).

The `to_numpy()` methods of `ArrowTensorArray` and `ArrowVariableShapedTensorArray` in `python/ray/data/_internal/tensor_extensions/arrow.py` read each row from the data buffer without checking whether the row is null.

### Versions / Dependencies

- Ray 2.59.0 (pip), and master at ce833083bc
- Python 3.12.15, Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL2)
- NumPy 2.2.6 and 2.5.4, pandas 3.0.6, PyArrow 26.0.0 (master: pandas 2.3.3, PyArrow 23.0.1)

### Reproduction script

```python
import numpy as np
import pyarrow as pa
import ray
from ray.data.extensions import ArrowTensorArray, ArrowVariableShapedTensorArray

fixed = ArrowTensorArray.from_numpy(np.array([[10.0, 11.0], [20.0, 21.0]]))
ragged = ArrowVariableShapedTensorArray.from_numpy(
    [np.array([[10.0, 11.0], [12.0, 13.0]]), np.array([[20.0, 21.0, 22.0]])]
)
# Row 1 is null in both columns, as after a left outer join with no match.
rows = pa.array([0, None, 1])
ds = ray.data.from_arrow(pa.table({"fixed": fixed.take(rows), "ragged": ragged.take(rows)}))

print(ds.take_all()[1])
for col in ["ragged", "fixed"]:
    try:
        print(col, ds.select_columns([col]).to_pandas()[col][1])
    except TypeError as e:
        print(col, "TypeError:", e)
```

Output with NumPy 2.2.6:

```text
{'fixed': None, 'ragged': None}
ragged 20.0
fixed TypeError: buffer is too small for requested array
```

With NumPy 2.5.4, `ragged` raises `TypeError: Use () not None as shape arguments` instead.

### Issue Severity

Medium: It is a significant difficulty but I can work around it.

issues.description: Null rows now hold no values in the tensor storage, but the null-free fast path of to_numpy still computes the data offset as self.offset * items_per_row, so a null-free slice taken after a null row silently reads shifted rows (from_numpy([t0, None, t2, t3])[2:3].to_numpy() returns t3). The fix commit uses the absolute first list offset (storage.offsets[0]) as the buffer offset.

prs.notes: Issue comes from a review body (no inline anchor). Lines 1019-1020 are the PR-added null_count gate that sends null-free slices to the fast path; line 1046 is the offset computation the fix changed. The same review also reported that under ARROW_NATIVE None rows read back as zeros (fixed in the same commit); omitted because it has no single clear anchor.

prs.body: ## Summary - Adds a "Show local images" toggle in PowerToys Settings (File Explorer > Markdown) - When enabled, renders images referenced via relative paths or local file paths in the Markdown preview pane - Serves validated local image files on a WebView2 virtual host (`https://localmdimages/`) directly from the handler's resource filter - Supports local paths and UNC/network share paths - Default: OFF (preserves existing behavior) - GPO support: Admins can force-enable or force-disable via Group Policy Fixes #40787 Fixes #3713 ## Security model | Scenario | Behavior | |----------|----------| | Setting OFF (default) | All images blocked, info bar shown. Raw HTML `src` is rewritten to `#` in this state too, so a `data:` image cannot render (it is resolved internally and never reaches the resource filter) | | Setting ON + relative path (`media/img.png`) | Resolved against .md directory, rendered if under that tree | | Setting ON + path traversal (`../../secret.png`) | Blocked — resolved with `Path.GetFullPath` and checked with `Path.GetRelativePath`, including percent-encoded traversal on the serving side | | Setting ON + junction/symlink below the allowed path | Blocked — each component of the resolved path is rejected if it carries `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint`, since lexical containment alone does not prevent redirection | | Setting ON + UNC relative path (`images/pic.png` on `\\server\share`) | Allowed within share root | | Setting ON + remote URL (`https://evil.com/track.png`) | Always blocked | | data:/javascript: URI | Always blocked, in both setting states | | `srcset` on a raw HTML `` | Attribute removed, in both setting states — its candidates are not validated by the `src` sanitizer | | Script execution | Always disabled (`IsScriptEnabled = false`) | | Mark-of-the-Web (MotW) | Explorer blocks preview of MotW-tagged files before our code runs (OS-level protection) | ## GPO Policy - Policy name: `MarkdownAllowLocalImages` - Registry: `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\PowerToys\MarkdownAllowLocalImages` (DWORD: 1=enabled, 0=disabled) - ADMX category: **PowerToys > File Explorer Preview** - Uses `getConfiguredValue()` (individual module setting pattern, no global utility fallback) ## Screenshots ### Settings UI — new toggle _"Show local images" toggle nested under the Markdown preview section (File Explorer add-ons). Captured from a Debug build of this branch (the Settings app only runs standalone in Debug builds):_ ### Settings UI — locked by GPO _With the `MarkdownAllowLocalImages` policy set to Disabled, the toggle is forced Off and grayed out, and the "managed by your organization" info bar appears:_ ### GPO in Group Policy Editor _New "File Explorer Preview" category under PowerToys, showing the policy and its description:_ ### GPO set to Enabled _Policy enabled state in gpedit.msc:_ ### Preview with local images rendered _Markdown preview with local image rendering enabled — relative path image renders:_ ### Info bar for blocked remote images _When the document contains remote (http/https) image URLs, they are always blocked and an info bar is shown:_ ### GPO disabled — all images blocked _With GPO set to disabled, all images (local and remote) are blocked. Info bar reads "Some pictures have been blocked...":_ ### Mark-of-the-Web protection _Files copied from a network source carry a Zone Identifier (MotW). Explorer blocks the preview entirely before our code runs — an OS-level security layer:_ ## Implementation Two layers were blocking images: 1. **Markdig AST layer** (`HTMLParsingExtension.cs`): replaced image URLs with `#` 2. **WebView2 layer** (`MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl.cs`): returned HTTP 403 for all non-HTML requests Changes: - `HTMLParsingExtension`: conditionally resolves markdown `![](path)` images to virtual host URLs with path traversal protection - `MarkdownHelper`: regex-rewrites relative `src=""` in raw HTML `` tags to virtual host URLs - `MarkdownPreviewHandlerControl`: serves `https://localmdimages/` requests in the `WebResourceRequested` handler — the URL is resolved back to a file path, re-validated for containment against the allowed base path (document directory, or share root for UNC), and the bytes are returned via `CreateWebResourceResponse` with the proper content type. Note: `SetVirtualHostNameToFolderMapping` is deliberately NOT used for images — WebView2 Runtime 150+ no longer serves files from UNC/network folder mappings (verified by A/B test on 150.0.4078.48); serving from the handler works uniformly for local and UNC paths - Settings UI: new toggle nested under the Markdown preview expander, with GPO lock support - Handler `Settings.cs`: reads `EnableMdLocalImages` via `SettingsUtils`, GPO override via `GPOWrapper` - GPO: `gpo.h` individual module setting, ADMX/ADML with `FileExplorerPreview` category ## Known limitation Peek also renders Markdown through `FilePreviewCommon.MarkdownHelper`, but calls it without the local-images arguments, so **Peek does not show local images even when the setting is enabled** — it keeps the existing behavior of blocking every image. prs.title: Add esql method to Saved Objects repository and client
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/kibana-team/issues/2946

- Adds `esql` method to `ISavedObjectsRepository` and `SavedObjectsClientContract` for executing ES|QL queries against saved objects
- Injects space/namespace security filtering via `EsqlQueryRequest.filter` using the same `getNamespacesBoolFilter()` pattern as `search`
- Strips encrypted attribute values from ES|QL results (replaces with `null`)
- Includes unit tests, tutorial documentation, and example plugin route
- Uses `@kbn/esql-language` `esql` tagged template with named param syntax (`${{ name: value }}`) for injection-safe query construction

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests pass: `yarn test:jest src/core/packages/saved-objects/api-server-internal/src/lib/apis/esql.test.ts`
- [ ] Typecheck passes for affected packages
- [ ] Manual verification: start Kibana with example plugins, call `/api/saved_objects_example/_esql_query`
- [ ] Verify namespace security: queries in space A should not return results from space B
- [ ] Verify encrypted attributes are stripped in response columns

<details>
<summary>PRD: ES|QL Search for Saved Objects</summary>

# PRD: ES|QL Search for Saved Objects

## Introduction

Add an `esql` method to the Saved Objects client and repository, following the same pattern as the existing `search` method ([PR #239432](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/239432)). Like `search`, the `esql` method avoids the translation/indirection layer of the `find` method to give consumers access to the full power of ES|QL's processing commands. The consumer specifies saved object types (as with `search` and `find`), and the system handles index resolution (via `getIndicesForTypes`) and security filtering (via `EsqlQueryRequest.filter`). The consumer writes only the ES|QL processing pipeline (everything after `FROM`), keeping index names as an implementation detail they never need to know.

### Prior Art

- **`find` method:** Exposes a saved-object-specific data model that translates queries and documents. This indirection requires rewriting the whole API surface of Elasticsearch.
- **`search` method** ([PR #239432](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/239432)): Avoids this translation to directly support the full ES `_search` DSL. Security is maintained by injecting a `namespacesBoolFilter` via `mergeUserQueryWithNamespacesBool`. Includes a [tutorial](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/241235) and [security best practices documentation](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/246064).
- **`esql` method (this PRD):** Repeats the `search` pattern but for ES|QL queries via Elasticsearch's `esql.query` API.

## Goals

- Add `esql` method to `ISavedObjectsRepository` and `SavedObjectsClientContract`
- Accept an ES|QL processing `pipeline` (everything after FROM) — the `FROM` clause is auto-generated from the `type` parameter via `getIndicesForTypes()`
- Inject space/namespace security filtering via the `EsqlQueryRequest.filter` parameter (includes type restriction — consumers don't need `WHERE type ==`)
- Enforce RBAC authorization using the same `securityExtension.authorizeFind` pattern as `search`
- Handle hidden types consistently with `search` and `find`
- Return raw ES|QL responses (`EsqlQueryResponse`) without translation
- Document usage, security risks, and the `@kbn/esql-language` `esql` tagged template composer for injection prevention

## User Stories

### US-001: Define `SavedObjectsEsqlOptions` types and add `esql` to `ISavedObjectsRepository`
**Description:** As a Kibana core developer, I want to define the ES|QL types and add an `esql` method to the saved objects repository interface so that plugins can execute ES|QL queries against saved objects with security enforced.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] New type file at `api-server/src/apis/esql.ts` defining `SavedObjectsEsqlOptions` and `SavedObjectsEsqlResponse`
- [ ] `SavedObjectsEsqlOptions` extends `Omit<estypes.EsqlQueryRequest, 'format' | 'columnar' | 'delimiter' | 'query'>`, adding:
  - `type: string | string[]` — saved object types to query (used for index resolution and security)
  - `namespaces: string[]` — spaces to query within
  - `pipeline: string` — the ES|QL processing pipeline (everything after FROM, e.g., `'| KEEP dashboard.title | LIMIT 100'`)
  - `metadata?: string[]` — optional METADATA fields on the FROM clause (e.g., `['_id', '_source']`)
- [ ] `SavedObjectsEsqlResponse` is a type alias for `estypes.EsqlQueryResponse` (aliased from `EsqlEsqlResult` in ES client types)
- [ ] `ISavedObjectsRepository` interface (in `api-server/src/saved_objects_repository.ts`) has a new `esql` method with signature: `esql(options: SavedObjectsEsqlOptions): Promise<SavedObjectsEsqlResponse>`
- [ ] Types are exported from `api-server/src/apis/index.ts` barrel and `api-server/index.ts`
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes

**Implementation notes:**
- The `query` field from `EsqlQueryRequest` is omitted because the full query is constructed internally by combining `FROM <indices>` (resolved from `type` via `getIndicesForTypes()`) with the consumer's `pipeline`
- Also omits `format`, `columnar`, and `delimiter` (not relevant for saved objects)
- `estypes.EsqlQueryResponse` is internally aliased to `EsqlEsqlResult` in the ES client types
- The `filter` field on `EsqlQueryRequest` is `QueryDslQueryContainer` — this is where security filters are injected (includes type restriction, so consumers don't need `WHERE type ==` in their pipeline)

### US-002: Add `esql` to `SavedObjectsClientContract`, mocks, and repository stub
**Description:** As a Kibana plugin developer, I want the `esql` method available on the saved objects client so that I can use it from route handlers via `ctx.core.savedObjects.client.esql()`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `SavedObjectsClientContract` interface (in `api-server/src/saved_objects_client.ts`) has the `esql` method with JSDoc warning about security risks (matching `search` method's remarks)
- [ ] `SavedObjectsClient` implementation (in `api-server-internal/src/saved_objects_client.ts`) delegates to the repository's `esql` method
- [ ] Repository mock (`api-server-mocks/src/repository.mock.ts`) includes `esql` as a jest mock
- [ ] Internal repository mock (`api-server-internal/src/mocks/repository.mock.ts`) includes `esql` as a jest mock — **there are TWO repository mock files that must stay in sync**
- [ ] Client mock (`api-server-mocks/src/saved_objects_client.mock.ts`) includes `esql` as a jest mock
- [ ] `SavedObjectsRepository` class gets a **stub** `esql` method (throws "not implemented") to satisfy the interface — the real implementation is wired in US-004
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes

**Implementation notes:**
- `SavedObjectsClient` in `api-server-internal` simply delegates to the repository, following the pattern of all other methods
- Adding a method to `ISavedObjectsRepository` requires updating the `SavedObjectsRepository` class immediately (even with a stub) to pass typecheck — the stub is replaced in US-004

### US-003: Implement `performEsql` in the repository internals
**Description:** As a Kibana core developer, I want the internal implementation of the `esql` method to execute ES|QL queries via the Elasticsearch client while injecting space and type security filters and auto-generating the FROM clause.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] New `performEsql` function in `api-server-internal/src/lib/apis/esql.ts`, following the pattern of `performSearch` in `search.ts`
- [ ] Accepts a `PerformEsqlParams` object with `options: SavedObjectsEsqlOptions` and `rawClient: ElasticsearchClient` (see implementation notes)
- [ ] Validates `options.namespaces` is not empty (throws `BadRequestError` if empty)
- [ ] Validates `options.type` contains at least one allowed type (returns empty response `{ columns: [], values: [] }` if none match `allowedTypes`)
- [ ] Resolves indices from types via `commonHelper.getIndicesForTypes(types)` and constructs the `FROM <indices>` clause (with optional `METADATA` fields if `options.metadata` is provided)
- [ ] Constructs the full ES|QL query by concatenating the FROM clause with the consumer's `pipeline`
- [ ] Validates that `pipeline` does not start with a source command (`FROM`, `ROW`, `SHOW`, `METRICS`) — throws `BadRequestError` if it does
- [ ] Uses `spacesExtension.getSearchableNamespaces()` to resolve authorized namespaces; returns empty response on 403 Boom errors
- [ ] Uses `securityExtension.authorizeFind()` to check RBAC, supporting `partially_authorized` via `typeToNamespacesMap`
- [ ] Constructs the namespaces bool filter via `getNamespacesBoolFilter()` (imported from `../search`) — this filter already includes type restriction
- [ ] Injects the filter into `EsqlQueryRequest.filter` — merging with any user-provided filter using `{ bool: { must: [namespacesBoolFilter, userFilter] } }`
- [ ] Calls `rawClient.esql.query()` with the constructed query and filter
- [ ] Returns the raw `EsqlQueryResponse`
- [ ] Exported from `apis/index.ts` barrel file
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes

**Implementation notes:**
- **Critical:** `RepositoryEsClient` only wraps top-level ES methods (`search`, `get`, `bulk`, etc.) — it does NOT expose `esql.query()`. The raw `ElasticsearchClient` must be passed separately via the `rawClient` parameter. It's available in the repository as `this.options.client`
- Index resolution uses `commonHelper.getIndicesForTypes(types)` — same as `search` and `find`. The FROM clause is constructed as `FROM ${indices.join(', ')}` (with `METADATA ${metadata.join(', ')}` appended if specified)
- The consumer's `pipeline` is appended to the FROM clause. If the pipeline starts with `|`, the full query is `FROM <indices> ${pipeline}`. If it doesn't start with `|`, prepend a space.
- `getNamespacesBoolFilter` and the filter-merging pattern can be reused directly from `search.ts`
- The namespace bool filter already restricts to the specified types — consumers don't need `WHERE type ==` in their pipeline
- ES|QL uses `filter` field (not `query`) for injecting security filters — this aligns with how `getNamespacesBoolFilter` works

### US-004: Wire `esql` into the repository implementation
**Description:** As a Kibana core developer, I want the repository class to delegate `esql` calls to the `performEsql` function with the correct execution context.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `SavedObjectsRepository.esql()` method (in `api-server-internal/src/lib/repository.ts`) replaces the stub with a call to `performEsql({ options, rawClient: this.options.client }, this.apiExecutionContext)`
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes

**Implementation notes:**
- Raw ES client is available via `this.options.client` in the repository (constructor stores options as `private readonly`)
- Prettier enforces single-line for short function calls — don't split across multiple lines

### US-005: Strip/redact encrypted attributes from ES|QL results
**Description:** As a Kibana core developer, I want encrypted saved object attributes to be stripped from ES|QL query results so that secrets are never exposed in tabular responses.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Add `getEncryptedAttributes(type: string): ReadonlySet<string> | undefined` to `ISavedObjectsEncryptionExtension` interface (in `server/src/extensions/encryption.ts`)
- [ ] Implement `getEncryptedAttributes` on `SavedObjectsEncryptionExtension` class (in `encrypted_saved_objects` plugin) — delegates to `EncryptedSavedObjectsService`
- [ ] Implement `getEncryptedAttributes` on `EncryptedSavedObjectsService` — returns the `ReadonlySet` from the type's definition stored in the private `Map`
- [ ] Update all three encryption extension mocks: `api-server-mocks`, `api-server-internal/mocks`, and ESO plugin service mocks
- [ ] Add `stripEncryptedColumns` function to `performEsql` that nulls encrypted column values
- [ ] ES|QL columns for SO attributes use the pattern `<type>.<attribute_name>` — match against this pattern to identify encrypted columns
- [ ] Replace values in encrypted columns with `null` (preserving column structure so row indices remain stable)
- [ ] If no encryption extension exists or all requested types are non-encryptable, skip post-processing entirely (fast path)
- [ ] Works correctly for mixed-type queries where only some types have encrypted attributes
- [ ] Document in the tutorial that encrypted fields are stripped (not decrypted) because ES|QL returns tabular data and AAD reconstruction from columns/values is not feasible
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes

**Implementation notes:**
- **Critical:** `ISavedObjectsEncryptionExtension` did NOT have `getEncryptedAttributes` — it must be added to the core interface AND implemented in the ESO plugin
- `EncryptedSavedObjectsService` stores type definitions in a private `Map`; `getEncryptedAttributes` returns the `ReadonlySet` from the definition
- Three encryption mock files need updating: `api-server-mocks/src/saved_objects_extensions.mock.ts`, `api-server-internal/src/mocks/saved_objects_extensions.mock.ts`, and `encrypted_saved_objects/server/crypto/encrypted_saved_objects_service.mocks.ts`

### US-006: Write unit tests for `performEsql`
**Description:** As a Kibana core developer, I want comprehensive unit tests so that I can verify the FROM clause generation, security filtering, authorization, encryption stripping, and error handling of the `esql` method.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Test file at `api-server-internal/src/lib/apis/esql.test.ts`
- [ ] Tests that the FROM clause is auto-generated from `type` via `getIndicesForTypes()`
- [ ] Tests that `metadata` fields are appended to the FROM clause (e.g., `FROM .kibana METADATA _id`)
- [ ] Tests that `pipeline` is appended after the FROM clause
- [ ] Tests that a pipeline starting with a source command (`FROM`, `ROW`, `SHOW`, `METRICS`) throws `BadRequestError`
- [ ] Tests that namespaces filter is injected into `EsqlQueryRequest.filter`
- [ ] Tests that user-provided `filter` is merged (not replaced) with the security filter
- [ ] Tests that empty `namespaces` throws `BadRequestError`
- [ ] Tests that unauthorized types return empty response
- [ ] Tests that `partially_authorized` correctly restricts types to authorized namespaces
- [ ] Tests that hidden types are filtered from allowed types
- [ ] Tests that encrypted attribute columns have their values replaced with `null`
- [ ] Tests that non-encrypted columns are returned unmodified
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes

**Implementation notes:**
- **Critical:** Must test through the `SavedObjectsRepository` class (not call `performEsql` directly) because `getNamespacesBoolFilter` from `../search` doesn't resolve correctly in direct Jest imports
- Follow the pattern of `search.test.ts`: use `@ts-expect-error` to access private constructor
- Use `client.esql.query.mockResolvedValue()` to mock ES|QL responses
- Verify the constructed `query` string passed to `client.esql.query()` includes the correct FROM clause + pipeline
- The ES client TypeScript types define `EsqlESQLParam` as `FieldValue | FieldValue[]` (positional), but ES also supports named params as `Record<string, unknown>` at runtime (the types are incomplete). The `@kbn/esql-language` composer produces named params.

### US-007: Write tutorial documentation
**Description:** As a Kibana plugin developer, I want a tutorial doc so that I can understand how to use the `esql` method, including the pipeline concept, security model, and the `esql` tagged template composer for avoiding injection attacks.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] New tutorial at `dev_docs/tutorials/saved_objects_esql.mdx` (following `saved_objects_search.mdx` pattern)
- [ ] Explains the relationship between `find`, `search`, and `esql` methods
- [ ] Explains the `pipeline` concept: consumers write only the ES|QL processing pipeline (everything after FROM), the system handles index resolution from `type` and security filtering. No `FROM` clause or `WHERE type ==` needed.
- [ ] Shows a basic usage example in a route handler (using `savedObjectsClient.esql()` with `pipeline`)
- [ ] Shows how to use `metadata` for `METADATA _id, _source` on the FROM clause
- [ ] Explains how space and type security filtering is injected via the `filter` parameter — emphasizes that the DSL filter already restricts to the specified types
- [ ] Documents the `esql` tagged template from `@kbn/esql-language` as the recommended way to build pipelines with user input — specifically the **named param syntax** `${{ name: value }}` which creates proper `?name` parameterized placeholders (code/data separation at the protocol level). The plain `${value}` syntax only provides quoting-based protection (inlines as escaped literal) which is less safe.
- [ ] Shows how to extract pipeline and params from the composer: use `.print()` for the pipeline string and `.getParams()` for the named params, converting to the format expected by `SavedObjectsEsqlOptions`
- [ ] Documents the type gap: the composer's `.toRequest()` method returns `{ filter?: unknown, params?: EsqlRequestParams }` which doesn't match the ES client's `{ filter?: QueryDslQueryContainer, params?: EsqlESQLParam[] }`. This is a TypeScript-level issue only — ES|QL named params work at runtime. Bridge with a type assertion or by extracting `.print()` + `.getParams()` separately
- [ ] Documents that encrypted fields are stripped (not decrypted) in responses
- [ ] Links to the Elasticsearch ES|QL documentation
- [ ] Typecheck/lint passes (mdx builds)

**Implementation notes:**
- The `@kbn/esql-language` `esql` composer has two template hole modes — document both clearly:
  1. **`${{ name: value }}`** (named param shorthand) — creates a `?name` placeholder in the query and stores the value in the params bag. This is true parameterization: code and data are separated at the protocol level. **This is the recommended approach for user input.**
  2. **`${value}`** (plain synth hole) — inlines the value into the query string as an escaped literal (strings get proper `"` quoting with `\` escaping via `LeafPrinter.string()`). Provides quoting-based protection but is NOT true parameterization. Acceptable for developer-controlled values, not for user input.
- The composer's `.toRequest()` types have a gap with the ES client types (`filter?: unknown` vs `QueryDslQueryContainer`, and `EsqlRequestParams` includes `Record<string, unknown>` entries while `EsqlESQLParam` is `FieldValue | FieldValue[]`). This is a TypeScript-level issue only — Elasticsearch supports named params at runtime. To bridge: either use a type assertion on `.toRequest()`, or extract `.print()` for query and convert `.getParams()` to the params array format manually.
- Existing codebase callers (e.g., `kbn-index-editor`) use the composer purely for query string construction via `.print()` and `.pipe`, not via `.toRequest()`. This is fine for developer-controlled values but doesn't leverage parameterization.
- Note: since the consumer writes only the pipeline (not a full query with FROM), the composer is used to build the pipeline string, not the full query. The FROM clause is added by `performEsql` internally.
- When simplifying examples, remember to remove unused package references from `tsconfig.json`

- [ ] Shows a simple pipeline example (e.g., `| KEEP dashboard.title | SORT dashboard.title | LIMIT 100`)
- [ ] Shows usage of `@kbn/esql-language` `esql` tagged template with named param synta…

prs.title: Fix GraphFlow to support multiple task execution without explicit reset
prs.body:
## Problem

When using GraphFlow with a termination condition, the second task execution would immediately terminate without running any agents. The first task would run successfully, but subsequent tasks would skip all agents and go directly to the stop agent.

This was demonstrated by the following issue:

```python
# First task runs correctly
result1 = await team.run(task="First task")  # ✅ Works fine

# Second task fails immediately  
result2 = await team.run(task="Second task")  # ❌ Only user + stop messages
```

## Root Cause

The `GraphFlowManager` was not resetting its execution state when termination occurred. After the first task completed:

1. The `_ready` queue was empty (all nodes had been processed)
2. The `_remaining` and `_enqueued_any` tracking structures remained in "completed" state
3. The `_message_thread` retained history from the previous task

This left the graph in a "completed" state, causing subsequent tasks to immediately trigger the stop agent instead of executing the workflow.

## Solution

Added an override of the `_apply_termination_condition` method in `GraphFlowManager` to automatically reset the graph execution state when termination occurs:

```python
async def _apply_termination_condition(
    self, delta: Sequence[BaseAgentEvent | BaseChatMessage], increment_turn_count: bool = False
) -> bool:
    # Call the base implementation first
    terminated = await super()._apply_termination_condition(delta, increment_turn_count)
    
    # If terminated, reset the graph execution state and message thread for the next task
    if terminated:
        self._remaining = {target: Counter(groups) for target, groups in self._graph.get_remaining_map().items()}
        self._enqueued_any = {n: {g: False for g in self._enqueued_any[n]} for n in self._enqueued_any}
        self._ready = deque([n for n in self._graph.get_start_nodes()])
        # Clear the message thread to start fresh for the next task
        self._message_thread.clear()
    
    return terminated
```

This ensures that when a task completes (termination condition is met), the graph is automatically reset to its initial state ready for the next task.

## Testing

Added a comprehensive test case `test_digraph_group_chat_multiple_task_execution` that validates:
- Multiple tasks can be run sequentially without explicit reset calls
- All agents are executed the expected number of times  
- Both tasks produce the correct number of messages
- The fix works with various termination conditions (MaxMessageTermination, TextMentionTermination)

## Result

GraphFlow now works like SelectorGroupChat where multiple tasks can be run sequentially without explicit resets between them:

```python
# Both tasks now work correctly
result1 = await team.run(task="First task")   # ✅ 5 messages, all agents called
result2 = await team.run(task="Second task")  # ✅ 5 messages, all agents called again
```

Fixes #6746.

prs.body: ## Overview This PR addresses Issue #43211 which is based on the main parent Issue #43211 by implementing two related improvements to the Azure Cosmos DB Python SDK: 1. **Make `max_concurrency` optional with adaptive ThreadPool default (sync only)** 2. **Fix `create_database` and `create_database_if_not_exists` overload signatures** ## Changes ### 1. Optional `max_concurrency` for Adaptive Resource Usage (Sync Path Only) **Problem:** The hardcoded default of `max_concurrency=10` was arbitrary and could be too high for resource-constrained systems or too low for high-core-count systems. **Solution:** Changed `max_concurrency` to `Optional[int]` with default `None` **for the sync path only**, allowing Python's ThreadPoolExecutor to use its adaptive default. **Modified files:** - `azure/cosmos/container.py` - `read_items()` method signature and docstring (sync) - `azure/cosmos/_read_items_helper.py` - Helper class initialization (sync) - `azure/cosmos/_cosmos_client_connection.py` - Client connection default and docstring (sync) **Example:** ```python # Sync: Uses adaptive default based on CPU cores items = container.read_items(items=[(id1, pk1), (id2, pk2)]) # Sync: Explicitly set workers items = container.read_items(items=[(id1, pk1)], max_concurrency=5) # Async: Continues to use default of 10 (uses asyncio.Semaphore) items = await container.read_items(items=[(id1, pk1), (id2, pk2)]) ``` ### 2. Fix `create_database` Overload Signatures **Problem:** The overloads were missing `response_hook` parameter, included the deprecated `populate_query_metrics`, and `offer_throughput` was not consistently keyword-only. **Solution:** Updated overload signatures for both sync and async versions: - ✅ Added `response_hook` parameter to all overloads - ✅ Removed `populate_query_metrics` from overload signatures (kept in implementation with deprecation warning) - ✅ Made `offer_throughput` keyword-only in sync overloads - ✅ Updated implementations to properly invoke `response_hook` **Modified files:** - `azure/cosmos/cosmos_client.py` - Sync versions - `azure/cosmos/aio/_cosmos_client.py` - Async versions **Example:** ```python # Recommended usage with keyword arguments db = client.create_database("mydb", offer_throughput=400) # Access response metadata with response_hook def log_charge(headers): print(f"RU charge: {headers.get('x-ms-request-charge')}") db = client.create_database("mydb", response_hook=log_charge) # Get both proxy and properties db_proxy, properties = client.create_database( "mydb", return_properties=True, response_hook=log_charge ) ``` ## Backward Compatibility ✅ **100% backward compatible** - All existing code continues to work: - Code using `max_concurrency=10` still works (both sync and async) - Code not specifying `max_concurrency` now gets adaptive behavior (better default) - `populate_query_metrics` still accepted in implementation (with deprecation warning) - `offer_throughput` can still be passed positionally in implementation ## Files Changed **Sync path (max_concurrency changes):** - `azure/cosmos/container.py` - Updated signature and docstring - `azure/cosmos/_read_items_helper.py` - Updated initialization - `azure/cosmos/_cosmos_client_connection.py` - Updated default and docstring **Both sync and async (create_database changes):** - `azure/cosmos/cosmos_client.py` - Updated overloads (sync) - `azure/cosmos/aio/_cosmos_client.py` - Updated overloads (async) **Tests:** - `tests/test_max_concurrency.py` - New file with 4 unit tests **Total: 6 files changed** Fixes Azure/azure-sdk-for-python#43268 --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Child issue of [Issue 43211](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/issues/43211)

This issue proposes two related improvements:

1. Make max_concurrency Optional for Default ThreadPool Usage
As described in the original parent issue, the current default value of max_concurrency=10 may be too high for systems with limited resources. To improve flexibility and align with Python’s native defaults, we should:

   -Change behavior so that max_concurrency is optional.
   -If not explicitly set by the user, fall back to the default value provided by Python’s                     ThreadPoolExecutor, which is 5 workers (see: https://docs.python.org/3/library/concurrent.futures.html#concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor).

The new overloads for create_database and create_database_if_not_exists are missing the response_hook argument. Additionally, the following cleanup and enhancements should be made:

Add response_hook to the overloads.
Remove populate_query_metrics from the method signature.
Make offer_throughput a keyword-only argument.


Suggested Implementation Steps:

1. Update method signatures to reflect optional max_concurrency.
2. Ensure fallback to Python’s default threadpool size when max_concurrency is not provided.
3. Modify overloads for create_database and create_database_if_not_exists:

    -Add response_hook.
    -Remove populate_query_metrics.
    -Make offer_throughput keyword-only.


4. Add/update unit tests to validate the new behavior.

- `uv version` (normal mode)
- `uv version --project .` (explicit project mode)

## Fix for Referenced Project Options Not Consulted for Synthetic Default Export Eligibility

✅ **All steps completed:**

## Summary

This PR fixes an issue where TypeScript doesn't check default imports from project reference `.d.ts` files.

### Changes

**Modified `canHaveSyntheticDefault` in `src/compiler/checker.ts`**:
- Keeps original `getImpliedNodeFormatForEmit` logic for node16/nodenext (lines 3787-3795)
- Added check for non-node16/nodenext cases (lines 3797-3810):
  - Only when `getImpliedNodeFormatForEmit` returns undefined
  - Only for declaration files from project references
  - Tries both `getRedirectFromSourceFile` and `getRedirectFromOutput` to find project references
  - Uses `host.getEmitModuleFormatOfFile(file)` to get the referenced project's module format
  - Disallows synthetic defaults when format is ES module (using range check: `ES2015 <= kind <= ESNext`)

**Key improvements**:
1. **Correct ES module range check**: Changed from `>= ModuleKind.ES2015` to `ModuleKind.ES2015 <= targetModuleKind && targetModuleKind <= ModuleKind.ESNext` to exclude Node16+ (100-199) and Preserve (200) which have higher numeric values but aren't pure ES modules.

2. **Robust redirect lookup**: Uses `getRedirectFromSourceFile || getRedirectFromOutput` since declaration files can be mapped either way depending on resolution context.

**Added test**: `referenced project with esnext module disallows synthetic default imports` validates the fix.

**Updated baselines**: Tests correctly show errors for project references while keeping node_modules permissive.

### Impact

```typescript
// lib/utils.ts (referenced project with module: "esnext")
export const test = () => "test";

// app/index.ts (references lib)
import Test from '../lib/utils';  // Now errors: TS1192 Module has no default export
```

Project references with ES modules get correct diagnostics. Node_modules packages remain permissive.

4. Updated the documentation to indicate that classmethods and staticmethods are now supported

This implementation handles both possible ordering of decorators, making the API more flexible for users.

Fixes #15838.

prs.title: Fix null check optimization for IQueryable/DbSet types in LINQ queries
prs.body:
Fixed issue where comparing `DbSet<T>`/`IQueryable<T>` to `null` in LINQ queries would fail with translation error, while ensuring we don't incorrectly optimize away null checks for variables that could legitimately be null.

## Root Cause

In EF Core 9.0, the funcletizer was rewritten (commit a2b8f2ce) to support precompiled queries. When a `MemberExpression` returns `IQueryable<T>`, it evaluates the member, extracts the queryable's `.Expression`, and inlines it into the main query. This causes `ids != null && ids.Contains(...)` to become `(db.Items.Select(...)) != null && (db.Items.Select(...)).Contains(...)`, where the null check comparing a `MethodCallExpression` to null fails translation.

## Changes Made

**Modified `NullCheckRemovingExpressionVisitor.cs`**:
- Added `TryOptimizeQueryableNullCheck()` method to detect and optimize IQueryable/DbSet null checks
- Added `IsNonNullableQueryExpression()` helper to identify expressions that are guaranteed non-null
- Only optimizes method calls, query roots, and DbSet property accesses (NOT parameters/variables)
- Optimizes `queryMethod() != null` → `true` and `queryMethod() == null` → `false`

**Added Tests in `NorthwindWhereQueryTestBase.cs`**:
- `Where_Queryable_not_null_check_with_Contains`: Tests `ids != null && ids.Contains(...)` where `ids` is always non-null
- `Where_Queryable_null_check_with_Contains`: Tests `ids == null || !ids.Contains(...)` where `ids` is always non-null
- `Where_Queryable_conditional_null_check_with_Contains`: Tests `ids != null && ids.Contains(...)` where `ids` could be null (conditional assignment)
- `Where_Queryable_conditional_null_check_with_Contains_negated`: Tests `ids == null || !ids.Contains(...)` where `ids` could be null (conditional assignment)

**Added SQL Server Test Overrides in `NorthwindWhereQuerySqlServerTest.cs`**:
- Overrides for all 4 tests with SQL assertion validation

The conditional tests use a `someFlag` parameter to verify that the optimization correctly handles cases where the IQueryable variable could legitimately be null, ensuring null checks work as expected.

## Test Results
- ✅ All Where_Queryable tests: 30 tests passed (Sqlite)
- ✅ All NorthwindWhere tests: 412+ tests passed (Sqlite)
- ✅ SQL Server overrides added for all 4 new tests

## **Description**

This PR adds a phone-country selector to the v2 KYC Basic Info screen in the ramp/deposit native flow. Previously the phone number's country code was locked to the user's geodetected/KYC region, so a user whose phone number belongs to a different country than their detected region could not enter a valid number.

The phone input and its country selector are encapsulated in a new reusable `PhoneField` component (mirroring the existing `DepositPhoneField` pattern), replacing the region-locked phone input that was previously inlined in the Basic Info screen. Tapping the flag/prefix accessory opens a new `PhoneCountrySelectorModal` — a searchable bottom-sheet list of countries with phone metadata (Fuse.js search over name, ISO code, and dialing prefix).

`PhoneField` keeps the full `mobileNumber` (dialing prefix + local digits) in form state and owns the phone-country selection independently of `userRegion`. The default phone country is derived by matching the previously entered `mobileNumber` against known country phone prefixes (longest match first), falling back to the user's region. A user's explicit pick takes precedence over that default. When the country changes, the local digits are re-prefixed with the newly selected country's dialing code and any stale phone-validation error is cleared. Typing a single digit never auto-advances the cursor; only a large jump in local digits (autofill/paste) advances to the next field. The existing `userRegion` behavior is intentionally preserved for region analytics and US SSN requirements — only the phone prefix is decoupled.

The selector is registered under its own dedicated `RampPhoneCountrySelectorModal` route in the ramp modals navigator (rather than reusing the region-selector route), and ships phone-specific copy via a new `deposit.phone_country_modal` i18n namespace translated across all supported locales. Unit tests cover the `PhoneField` component, the prefix/inference helpers, the `PhoneCountrySelectorModal`, and the updated Basic Info flow.

## **Changelog**

linked_issues.body:
## Problem

Claude Code exports OpenTelemetry **traces** with **custom** span attribute keys (for example `span.type`, `user_prompt`, token fields, and `model`) instead of the GenAI semantic conventions Latitude likely assumes. As a result, Claude Code sessions can appear in Latitude with missing or empty prompts, token usage, and model metadata—even when that data is present on the spans.

## Impact

- Users tracing Claude Code cannot reliably see user prompts, model names, or token-related fields in the product.
- Usage and cost signals that Claude Code attaches to spans may not surface in Latitude’s trace views or downstream analytics.

## Context: example span attributes (Claude Code)

These are illustrative shapes keyed by `span.type` (not exhaustive).

**`interaction`** (user turn metadata):


```json

  "attempt": 1,
  "cache_creation_tokens": 4797,
  "cache_read_tokens": 11229,
  "duration_ms": 1991,
  "input_tokens": 3,
  "llm_request.context": "interaction",
  "model": "claude-opus-4-6[1m]",
  "organization.id": "40e41a65-f41c-4b27-8de7-3f1fbe173d65",
```

**Note:** Claude Code may also emit richer message content via **OTLP logs** (separate signal from traces). This issue focuses on **trace** attribute handling; full log ingestion can be tracked separately if needed.

## Proposed Solution

Treat Claude Code as a first-class trace shape: recognize `span.type`-driven spans (`interaction`, `llm_request`, and related types as discovered), map or normalize the custom attributes into Latitude’s internal representation (and/or UI) so prompts, model, token counts, cache token fields, duration, TTFT, and success surface consistently. Use `session.id` (and standard trace correlation) to relate interaction and LLM spans within a session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Traces from Claude Code show user-visible prompt text where `user_prompt` (or equivalent) is present on interaction spans.
- [ ] LLM request spans surface model name and token-related fields (including cache read/creation when present) in Latitude’s trace UX or normalized model consistent with other providers.
- [ ] Spans remain correctly correlated within a session/trace (e.g. via `session.id` and parent/child relationships).
- [ ] Automated tests or fixtures cover at least one `interaction` and one `llm_request` attribute payload shape.

prs.title: feat: enrich PostHog person records for machine identities
prs.body: ## Context Machine identity person records in PostHog (those with `identity-{uuid}` distinct IDs) are created automatically when events like `SecretPulled` are captured, but they lack any useful properties — no name, no auth method, just a bare ID. This is because `postHog.identify()` is only called for human users today (via `identifyUser`), never for machine identities. This PR adds an `identifyIdentity()` function to the telemetry service and calls it during `IDENTITY_ACCESS_TOKEN` authentication, enriching machine identity person records with `name` and `authMethod`. **Key design decisions:** - **Machine-identity-only by construction**: `identifyIdentity` builds the distinctId internally as `identity-${identityId}`, so it cannot accidentally enrich a real user's person record. - **Cloud-only gating**: Same `InstanceType.Cloud` check as `identifyUser`. - **In-memory dedup**: A `Map` with 10-minute TTL entries prevents calling `postHog.identify()` on every single authenticated request. The dedup key includes both `identityId` and `authMethod` so auth method changes are reflected immediately. On error, the timeout handle is cleared and the entry is removed to allow retries. Timers are `.unref()`-ed so they don't block graceful shutdown. This is per-instance (not shared across replicas), which is fine since `identify()` is idempotent. - **Fire-and-forget**: Called with `void` in the auth hook to avoid blocking request processing. ## Updates since initial revision Addressed Greptile review feedback across multiple rounds: - **Dedup key now includes `authMethod`**: Previously keyed only by `identityId`, which meant if the same identity authenticated with different auth methods within the TTL window, only the first `authMethod` would reach PostHog. Now keyed by `${identityId}-${authMethod}`. - **`clearTimeout` on error**: The `setTimeout` handle is now stored and cancelled in the catch block, preventing stale timers from prematurely expiring re-added entries after a retry. - **`timer.unref()`**: Dedup timers are now unref'd so they don't prevent graceful process exit during shutdown (since `flushAll` only calls `postHog.shutdownAsync()` and does not clear the dedup map). - Switched from `Set` to `Map` to store timer handles. ## Important things for reviewer to verify 1. **`identity.identityName` vs `identity.name`**: The code passes `identity.identityName` as the PostHog `name` property. Greptile confirmed this is the correct field — it resolves to the identity's display name via the DAL join on the `Identity` table, distinct from `identity.name` which is the access token's own optional label. Worth verifying independently. 2. **Auth path coverage**: Only the `IDENTITY_ACCESS_TOKEN` case in `inject-identity.ts` is instrumented. If machine identities can authenticate via other auth modes, those paths would not be enriched. 3. **Pre-existing inconsistency (not introduced here)**: `identityAuthInfo.identityName` at `inject-identity.ts:229` is set to `identity.name` (nullable token label) rather than `identity.identityName` (display name). PostHog now receives the correct value while the request context carries a potentially `undefined` name — worth a follow-up fix. ## Steps to verify the change 1. Authenticate as a machine identity using an identity access token against a Cloud instance 2. Check PostHog for the `identity-{uuid}` person record — it should now have `name` and `authMethod` properties set ## Type - [ ] Fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Improvement - [ ] Breaking - [ ] Docs - [ ] Chore ## Checklist - [x] Title follows the [conventional commit](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary) format - [ ] Tested locally - [ ] Updated docs (if needed) - [ ] Updated CLAUDE.md files (if needed) - [x] Read the [contributing guide](https://infisical.com/docs/contributing/getting-started/overview) --- [Link to Devin Session](https://app.devin.ai/sessions/f60882fcc61c491ab00e59ce7ee3f584) Requested by: @0xArshdeep ---

The phone-setup e2e test fails because the macOS app can't find the lockfile or the API key written by the test fixture, causing it to show the auth/onboarding screen instead of connecting to the already-hatched assistant.

prs.title: Keep nested JSDoc properties after a property with a missing name
prs.body:
Fixes #65020

When a nested `@property` type does not parse, every nested property after it is lost. With this change they are kept, as they are in flat typedefs and in TS 6.

```js
/**
 * @typedef Sig
 * @property {object} Args
 * @property {string} Args.name
 * @property {function(string)=} Args.onSave
 * @property {((v: string) => void)=} Args.onCancel
 */
```

- Before: `keyof Sig['Args']` is `"name"`.
- After: `keyof Sig['Args']` is `"" | "name" | "onCancel"`. The `TS1005` on `function(` stays.

## Cause

The type parse stops at `(`, so the name of the `Args.onSave` tag is a missing identifier. `parseChildParameterOrPropertyTag` reads a plain identifier name as the start of a new top-level property, so it ended the `Args` type literal there. `Args.onSave` and `Args.onCancel` were then parsed at the typedef level.

The fix skips that check when the name is missing, so the tag stays in the nested literal. That gives the same `""` property that a flat typedef gets for the same tag.

## Test

`jsdocNestedPropertyTagInvalidType.ts` has a nested and a flat typedef with the same broken property, and `keyof` checks in a `.ts` file. Without the fix it reports `TS2322` and `TS2339` for `onCancel`.

`npx hereby test` passes with no other baseline changes. `hereby lint` and `hereby check:format` pass.
