linked_issues.title: Workflow actions still run after a filter step halts the run (workflow_log result=halted, asset archived/added to album anyway)
linked_issues.body:
### I have searched the existing issues, both open and closed, to make sure this is not a duplicate report.

- [x] Yes

### The bug

A workflow's action steps still run after an earlier filter step has stopped the run. The workflow log records the run as `halted` on the filter step (step 0), but the asset is still archived and/or added to the album configured in the following steps.

This has happened on two separate occasions with two different filter types (`assetFileFilter` and `assetTagFilter`), so the problem looks like it sits in how the run stops or how actions are dispatched, not in any one filter.

This is **not** #31953: we use `matching: "all"`, and the filter returns the correct result, because the run is logged as `halted`. It is also not #30625, which is a hard error. Here nothing errors; the action just runs anyway.

**Occurrence 1: controlled reproduction (20 Sep 2026)**

Workflow, trigger `AssetCreate`, logging enabled:

| order | method | config |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `immich-plugin-core#assetFileFilter` | `{"pattern": "screenshot", "matchType": "contains", "caseSensitive": false}` |
| 1 | `immich-plugin-core#assetArchive` | `{"inverse": false}` |
| 2 | `immich-plugin-core#assetAddToAlbums` | `{"albumIds": ["<album>"]}` |

- Uploaded `cttest1.jpg`, a 64x64 solid-colour JPEG whose name does not contain "screenshot".
- `workflow_log` recorded exactly one run for the asset, `result = halted`, on the `assetFileFilter` step.
- The asset was nevertheless **archived and added to the album**.
- Control: with the workflow disabled, the same kind of upload (`cttest2.jpg`) stayed in the timeline and was not added to the album. Nothing else on the server (client, importer, other workflows) caused it.

Before the test this had been archiving ordinary iPhone camera photos (`IMG_xxxx.HEIC`) into the Screenshots album for several days.

**Occurrence 2: tag filter (5 Oct 2026)**

Two workflows, trigger `AssetCreate`, logging enabled:

| workflow | order | method | config |
|---|---|---|---|
| Add to Portfolio | 0 | `assetTagFilter` | `{"tags": ["<Portfolio tag>"], "matching": "all"}` |
| | 1 | `assetAddToAlbums` | `{"albumIds": ["<Portfolio album>"]}` |
| Add to Favourites | 0 | `assetTagFilter` | `{"tags": ["<Favourites tag>"], "matching": "all"}` |
| | 1 | `assetAddToAlbums` | `{"albumIds": ["<Favourites album>"]}` |

- Uploaded 65 JPEGs using the Lightroom Immich publish plugin.
- `workflow_log`: 130 runs (65 per workflow), **all `result = halted` at step 0**.
- Yet every one of the 65 assets was added to **both** albums. Only 3 assets actually carry the Portfolio tag and only 6 carry the Favourites tag.
- The same 65 files had been uploaded about 20 minutes earlier, before these two workflows existed. That earlier batch was not added to either album.
- Both workflows have since been disabled. I have not re-uploaded since to confirm the control for this occurrence; the disabled-workflow control from occurrence 1 is the A/B evidence.

Side note: the 9 tagged assets were also logged as `halted`. That suggests tags read from XMP/IPTC keywords are not attached yet when `AssetCreate` fires, so on upload a tag filter only sees the asset's tags at that moment. That may be expected (`AssetTagged` exists for this), but it would be worth documenting.

**Timing observation, not isolated:** for the same asset, `album_asset."createdAt"` is 11–60 ms **earlier** than the `workflow_log."createdAt"` row recording the halt. Asset creation to log row is about 40 ms. So either the action is dispatched before or alongside the filter step, or the log row is only written after the actions have already run. I read `workflow-execution.service.ts` and the step ordering, and both look correct, so I have not pinned down the mechanism.

Queries used:

```sql
SELECT w.name, l.result, s."order" AS step, count(*)
FROM workflow_log l
JOIN workflow w ON w.id = l."workflowId"
LEFT JOIN workflow_step s ON s.id = l."workflowStepId"
GROUP BY 1,2,3;
-- Add to Favourites | halted | 0 | 65
-- Add to Portfolio  | halted | 0 | 65

SELECT s."order", s.enabled, m.name, s.config
FROM workflow_step s JOIN plugin_method m ON m.id = s."pluginMethodId"
WHERE s."workflowId" = '<id>' ORDER BY s."order";
```

### The OS that Immich Server is running on

Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Docker inside a Proxmox LXC container)

### Version of Immich Server

v3.2.1 (`immich-plugin-core@2.0.1`). Not yet retested on v3.2.4.

### Version of Immich Mobile App

N/A (server-side workflows; the uploads came from the web and the Lightroom publish plugin)

### Platform with the issue

- [x] Server
- [ ] Web
- [ ] Mobile

### Device make and model

N/A

### Your docker-compose.yml content

```YAML
Standard release docker-compose.yml (immich-server, immich-machine-learning, ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0, valkey:9). The only change is a mem_limit on machine-learning.
```

```Shell
Standard; not relevant to workflow execution.
```

### Reproduction steps

1. Create a workflow on `AssetCreate` with logging enabled. Step 0 is a filter that will **not** match the upload, for example `assetFileFilter` with `contains "screenshot"`. Step 1 is `assetAddToAlbums` and/or `assetArchive`.
2. Upload an image whose filename does not match.

prs.title: fix(llms): revert implicit output cap regression
prs.body:
This fixes a regression in the SDK/apps/cli ChatGPT OAuth provider where starting a chat and sending a message could fail with:

```text
Error: unsupported parameter: max_output_tokens
```

Regression source:

- The regression was introduced by Robin's PR #10946, commit `2508e76af`, `Fix SDK model catalog token-limit semantics ENG-2100`.
- The useful part of that PR was catalog-side: it preserved provider-reported output limits instead of inventing small generated catalog caps. This PR keeps that behavior.
- The breaking part was request-side: the SDK gateway started converting catalog metadata into a concrete `request.maxTokens` value even when the caller did not configure one.
- `ai-sdk.ts` already forwarded any defined `request.maxTokens` as AI SDK `maxOutputTokens`.
- Once the gateway began synthesizing `request.maxTokens`, the OpenAI Responses adapter serialized it as `max_output_tokens`.
- The ChatGPT OAuth Codex backend at `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` rejects that parameter, so the first message could fail before a response streamed.

What this PR changes:

- Removes the implicit gateway default output cap from the request path.
- Keeps model catalog `maxTokens` as model capability metadata, not as an automatic provider request parameter.
- Only resolves and forwards `request.maxTokens` when a caller or host configuration explicitly provides a max output cap.
- Still clamps an explicit max output cap against the catalog model output limit and estimated remaining context window.
- Updates the AI SDK request construction so `maxOutputTokens` is omitted entirely when `request.maxTokens` is absent.
- Adds a dedicated ChatGPT OAuth regression test asserting that `openai-codex` requests do not include `maxOutputTokens` when the request omitted max tokens.

Why this is a partial revert instead of a full revert:

- A full revert of #10946 would throw away the catalog correctness work.
- The actual regression was the new behavior that treated catalog metadata as request intent.
- This PR reverts that behavior while preserving the catalog metadata semantics from Robin's PR.

What should be investigated next:

- Whether the SDK should have a product-level default max output cap at all, and if so where that default should be expressed.
- Whether default output caps should be host-owned, provider-owned, model-owned, or caller-owned rather than synthesized globally in the gateway.
- Whether provider manifests need explicit transport capability metadata for request parameters like `maxOutputTokens`, so future request-policy work can avoid provider-id checks and avoid assuming Responses-shaped backends support every OpenAI Responses field.
- Whether ChatGPT OAuth Codex should eventually support `max_output_tokens`, or whether the SDK should permanently treat that backend as a Responses-like but not fully Responses-compatible transport.
- Whether live provider tests should include a minimal ChatGPT OAuth smoke test for unsupported request parameters.

prs.title: fix(e2b, blaxel): S3 mount race condition and partial credential validation
prs.body:
Two bugs in S3 FUSE mounting for E2B and Blaxel sandboxes: concurrent mounts could corrupt each other's credentials file, and partial credential pairs (only `accessKeyId` or only `secretAccessKey`) failed silently or with cryptic errors.

## Changes

- **E2B – credentials path race condition**: Was using a shared `/tmp/.passwd-s3fs` for all mounts. Concurrent mounts to different buckets would overwrite each other's credentials mid-mount. prs.author: Winoren
prs.title: Python: fix(python): reject dot-segment remote paths in SessionsPythonTool.upload_file
prs.body:
### Motivation and Context

`download_file` rejects `.` and `..` path segments in the remote file name (#14520). The upload direction of the same plugin never got the equivalent guard: `_construct_remote_file_path` only prefixed `/mnt/data/` and passed the rest through, so a model-supplied `remote_file_path` of `../../escape.txt` was transmitted to the sessions service as `/mnt/data/../../escape.txt`.

The two directions of one plugin therefore disagreed on the same input, and the permissive one is reachable straight from a tool call:

```
LLM tool call: upload_file(remote_file_path="../../escape.txt", local_file_path=<allowed dir>)
  upload_file                  -> _validate_local_path_for_upload   (local side only, passes)
  upload_file                  -> _construct_remote_file_path        ("/mnt/data/../../escape.txt")
  http_client.post(files={"file": (remote_file_path, ...)})         -> leaves the process
```

`remote_file_path` is a string supplied by the model, not a path object, so nothing between the tool argument and the request body rejects the segments. Local validation cannot help here, which is why #13478's `allowed_upload_directories` check does not cover this case.

### Description

Applies the guard in the same helper `download_file` uses, with the same exception type and the same split on `/`, so the check cannot drift from the download side again:

```python
if any(segment in (".", "..") for segment in remote_file_path.split("/")):
    raise FunctionExecutionException("The remote file path must not contain '.' or '..' path segments.")
```

Placing it in `_construct_remote_file_path` rather than inline in `upload_file` means any future caller is covered by default.

### Testing

- New cases extend the existing `test_sessions_python_plugin.py`; no new file.
- The 9 malicious inputs (`"."`, `".."`, `"../x"`, `"../../x"`, `"./x"`, `"nested/./x"`, `"nested/../x"`, `"nested/.."`, `"/mnt/data/../../x"`) fail with `DID NOT RAISE` when the guard is reverted, and pass with it in place.
- 3 further cases assert ordinary paths still upload unchanged, including a nested path, an already-prefixed path, and they pass **both** with and without the fix, so they guard against over-rejection rather than coupling to the change.
- Over a 12-case differential sweep, 10 inputs are byte-identical before and after. The only behavior change is rejecting the dot segments. Legitimate names are untouched, including `.hidden.txt` and `a..b/c.txt`, since neither is a standalone `.` or `..` segment.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy` are clean on both files.

Note on the local test run: the errors seen in this file's fixtures are reproducible on unmodified `main` in my environment (a local dependency gap), so they are not caused by this change.

### One thing I did not change

`SessionsPythonPlugin.UploadFileAsync` on the .NET side has the same gap - it only does `Verify.NotNullOrWhiteSpace(remoteFileName)`. I kept this PR to the Python side to stay reviewable and single-purpose, since your recent work on this plugin has paired .NET and Python (e.g. #14085, #14140). Happy to extend it if you would rather land both together.

prs.body:
Fixes #12213.

When a `wrapModelCall` middleware returns a `Command` without calling `handler`, and an outer middleware returns that result unchanged, `AgentNode` collected the same `Command` instance once per middleware layer, so its update was applied once per layer. Added a test with the repro from the issue (outer pass-through, inner short-circuit `Command` on a `LastValue` field). It fails on `main` with `InvalidUpdateError` and passes with this change.

**Related command**

`az containerapp update --yaml` silently drops `identity.userAssignedIdentities` from the PATCH it sends. A manifest declaring

```yaml
identity:
  type: UserAssigned
  userAssignedIdentities:
    "/subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities/<uami>": {}
```

is sent (per `--debug`) as `"identity": {"type": "UserAssigned"}`.

```
>>> clean_null_values({'type': 'UserAssigned', 'userAssignedIdentities': {'/subscriptions/s/.../userAssignedIdentities/id': {}}})
{'type': 'UserAssigned'}
```

This affects `update_containerapp_yaml` here and the `containerapp` extension's `ContainerAppUpdateDecorator.set_up_update_containerapp_yaml`, which imports the same function. `az containerapp create --yaml` does not call it and is unaffected.


linked_issues.title: web-app: unguarded `localStorage` access in `AppPage.tsx` breaks the report in sandboxed contexts
linked_issues.body:
**Problem**

We host ORT reports in a web dashboard and serve the HTML with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts; …`, so that report content is isolated from the dashboard. We deliberately don't add `allow-same-origin`, because that would give the report the dashboard's origin and session. In this sandbox the page has an opaque origin, where any `localStorage` access throws `SecurityError: The operation is insecure`, and the report fails to load.

**Cause**

`AppPage.tsx` reads and writes `localStorage["ort-sidebar-collapsed"]` without `try/catch`, in the `useState` initializer and the `useEffect`. The throw happens during render. `lib/settings.ts` and the `history.replaceState` call already handle this case.

**Suggested fix**

Wrap both accesses in `try/catch`. If storage is unavailable, keep the sidebar state in memory only (`useState` already does this) and default `collapsed` to `false`. The only loss is that the preference isn't remembered across reloads.
